newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa market grapples with strong sterling.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa market grapples with strong sterling.

text.p: Sterling strength paralysed much of the German cocoa market as pound-denominated futures made local prices unattractive to buyers, traders said on Wednesday.
Sterling hit a fresh 52-month high of 2.7190 late on Tuesday. The Frankfurt midday fixing saw it at 2.7125.
"Consumers are sidelined as any price falls in London are wiped out by the currency trends," one trader said.
Manufacturer buying was also affected by preparations for the annual ISM confectionery fair in Cologne, which runs Jan 26-30.
The event, where national and international companies display new products and agree annual supply contracts, should offer clues to raw material ordering in 1997.
"Chocolate plants are running well at the moment and the Easter business should not be bad," another trader said.
"It looks as if Germany's cocoa grind in the first quarter could be back to normal."
Operators were surprised when the German fourth quarter 1996 figure was down by 21.7 percent from a year earlier, but later cited temporary plant problems and strikes.
In the market, traders said Ivory Coast arrival figures remained tentative, whereas in previous years data had begun to look reliable in the fourth quarter.
"I suspect it masks a rather bearish scenario -- sellers are knocking on our doors, buyers are well stocked -- nobody cares about theoretical supply deficits on paper," one said.
First quarter cif Ivorian bean sellers were little changed from last week at 2.31 marks per kg versus 2.28 last week. Second quarter beans were at 2.36.
The first quarter cocoa butter ratio was down three points at 2.65, with implied prices ex-works at 6.29 (6.30) marks per kg. Some spot sales were reported on a 2.63/2.64 basis.
Second quarter butter was also at a ratio of 2.65, with Wednesday's mark price at 6.38.
